meta.title: {brand} · Reproducible pipelines and governance for neural data
meta.description: Versioned, comparable pipelines and neural-data governance, from electrode to model. In development; for research and development use.

hero.heading: The data layer for brain-computer interfaces.
hero.sub: Versioned, comparable pipelines and neural-data governance, from electrode to model.

formats.note: Open formats and protocols, not partners.

pipeline.heading: One pipeline, from electrode to model.
pipeline.lede: Four stages. Every run is versioned, and every parameter, version and input hash is recorded as provenance.

steps.heading: Hardware-agnostic ingest
steps.body: Connectors for EEG, ECoG and microelectrode recordings in open formats, stored on standard time-series infrastructure.

steps.heading: Reproducible, comparable pipelines
steps.body: Versioned preprocessing pipelines with full provenance. Run one, or run a grid of them and see how your results move.

evidence.text: In a 2025 study, every artifact-correction step reduced decoding performance.
A 2025 comparison of 43 preprocessing pipelines found no single best pipeline.

steps.heading: Governed model registry
steps.body: Governed model registry (roadmap): versioned models with provenance, documented intended use and use restrictions. Benchmarks will be published with methods.

steps.heading: Python first, one shared core
steps.body: A Python SDK first, built on one shared core so every language records provenance the same way. C and C++ bindings follow; game engines on request.

code.heading: Every run carries its provenance.
code.body: Open a recording, run a pinned pipeline version, and get a provenance handle that records every parameter, version and input hash.
lines: import {pkg} as nf            # Illustrative API, subject to change
print(run.provenance.id)          # every parameter, version and input hash

governance.heading: Neural-data law is here. Govern the data, not just the files.
governance.lede: US states define neural data differently, so one recording can be regulated in one state and not in the next. Classification, consent and deletion have to follow the data into every derivative.

points.heading: Per-jurisdiction classification
points.body: Each channel and derived feature is classified against each state's definition.

points.heading: Versioned consent ledger
points.body: Opt-in consent recorded with its version, and withdrawal propagated to raw data, derivatives and trained models.

points.heading: Use restrictions on models
points.body: Models carry intended-use and use-restriction metadata, for example for EU workplace and education settings.

evidence.text: Colorado, California, Montana and Connecticut have passed laws that add neural data to the sensitive data their privacy laws protect; Connecticut's amendments carry July 1, 2026 effective dates.
Colorado and California cover the central or peripheral nervous system; Connecticut covers the central nervous system only; California excludes data inferred from non-neural information.

audience.heading: Built for labs and for device makers.
audience.lede: The same provenance and governance layer, packaged for two different jobs.

panels.heading: Spend your grant on science, not plumbing.
panels.body: Open your lab's recordings in a pipeline that other labs can re-run exactly, and compare pipelines instead of trusting one default.

bullets.text: Versioned pipelines you can cite and rerun
Export to MNE- and EEGLAB-compatible formats

panels.heading: You build the device. We carry the evidence.
panels.body: For neurotech teams that need traceable data, consent records and documentation their reviewers can follow.

bullets.text: Consent and deletion records per US state
Provenance for every parameter, version and input hash
White-label SDK on the shared core
Cloud deployment first; edge deployment on request

compliance.heading: Neural data is sensitive. Our design starts there.
compliance.lede: Controls listed with their current status. We hold no certifications and claim none.

rows.description: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit
Designed for HIPAA-aligned workflows. BAA available for enterprise (planned)
Built to support emerging US state neural-data privacy laws (e.g. Colorado, California, Connecticut, Montana)

claim.text: Colorado, California, Montana and Connecticut have enacted neural-data provisions in their consumer privacy laws.

rows.description: De-identification tooling to strip identifiers before sharing or export

compliance.legal: This is not legal advice. Customers remain responsible for their own regulatory obligations.

pricing.heading: Free for science. Fair for startups.
pricing.lede: No prices are final. We set them after discovery interviews, and early-access members hear first.

tiers.name: Academic
tiers.who: For individual researchers and students, with fair-use limits.

tiers.name: Startup
tiers.who: For seed-stage neurotech teams. Pricing at launch.

features.text: Consent and deletion ledger for core US states

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.who: For organizations with regulated data and dedicated needs.

research.heading: Whitepapers and working notes.

cards.summary: Modelling how patterned stimulation of somatosensory cortex could encode touch, pressure and proprioception.
cards.banner: Computational/theoretical work; any clinical application requires IRB/FDA oversight

cards.title: A reference architecture for HIPAA-aligned neural data pipelines
